title: OSHA Eyewash Station Checklist (29 CFR 1910.151)
subtitle: Use during routine site inspections and after any change in chemicals, processes or work areas.
instructions: Mark every item OK, Defect or N/A, and note the location you checked.
For each Defect, record the corrective action, who owns it and the due date, and recheck it once fixed.
The equipment manufacturer's instructions and your site rules may add checks to this list.

sections.title: Eyewash and drench facilities
items: Each area where eyes or body could contact injurious corrosive materials is listed, and each listed area has a flushing or drenching facility.
A unit that can quickly flush the eyes is installed at each listed area.
Where the body (not only the eyes) could be exposed, a unit that can quickly drench the body is installed.
The unit sits in the same work area as the corrosive hazard, not in another room or building.
Nothing blocks the route to the unit or its controls; a person can reach and operate it straight away.
When activated as the manufacturer describes, the unit delivers flushing fluid at once and without fault.
The unit is connected or filled, its supply is not shut off, and it is not tagged out of service.
Contractors, visitors and other people working near the corrosives can reach and use the unit.

sections.title: Medical personnel and first aid responders
items: Names and contact details of medical personnel who can advise and consult on plant health are posted or on record.
Records show whether an infirmary, clinic or hospital close to the workplace is used to treat all injured employees.
Where no such nearby facility treats every injured employee, one or more named people adequately trained to render first aid are on site, with training records.

sections.title: First aid supplies and kits
items: First aid kits are in known, unlocked, easy-to-reach locations.
Kits are stocked, items are usable, and contents meet the site's assessed needs.
For larger or multiple operations at one location, the number of kits, types of equipment and quantities have been assessed and provided (Appendix A guidance).
A dated review of first aid needs exists, drawing on the OSHA 300 log, OSHA 301 log or other injury reports (Appendix A guidance).
Where blood exposure during first aid is reasonably anticipated, gloves and other appropriate PPE such as face shields, masks or eye protection are kept with the kits (Appendix A; 1910.1030(d)(3)).

references: 29 CFR 1910.151: Medical services and first aid, including non-mandatory Appendix A (First aid kits)
